Comments: On 03/19/2021, Department of Environmental Protection ("DEP") representative John Ciccone conducted an administrative inspection for Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s ("CALLC") TANNER & HANA location at 0755 hours. This report is in response to CALLC’s Notice of Violation ("NOV") response for violations cited on 02/25/2021 against well permit # 015-23612. Details regarding the initial inspection can be found within inspection report # 3153908. On 03/16/2021, CALLC sent an electronic copy of their NOV response to the DEP satisfying the requirements of 25 Pa. Code 78a.66(c)(2(i). CALLC’s report stated demobilization operations resulted in the spreading of oil based muds ("OBM") beyond the extent of containment boundaries. A release volume estimate was not explicitly stated but is assumed to be greater than one barrel (42 gallons). Approximately 100 barrels of fluid (assumed > 1 barrel OBM and stormwater mixture) was vacuumed and recycled in CALLC’s completions operations. Approximately 16 tons of excavated fill material was disposed of as Residual Waste on 03/04/2021. On 03/08/2021, CALLC’s contractor, Creston Environmental ("Creston") collected 12 post-excavations samples. Sample results are still pending at this time. CALLC plans to document additional remedial action, associated attainments results, and restoration within an Act 2 deliverable, under direction of 25 Pa. Code 250 (Pennsylvania’s Land Recycling Program) and associated Land Recycling and Environmental Remediation Standards Act. CALLC’s NOV response has been uploaded to eFACTS with this report.

Comments: On 4/09/2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) inspection of Diversified's Chess 7 plugged well site located in Georges Township , Fayette County.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 6/03/2025. Therefore the well site restoration was due by 3/03/2026. A Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) is due by 5/03/2026.The following was observed during the inspection:The former access road and well site has not yet achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. Temporary E and S controls are installed on site. The site E and S/Restoration plans are available on site. No surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the approximate location of the plugged well. No plugging monument was observed on site during this inspection. Based on observations from this inspection, the restoration deadline has passed and the well site and access road are not restored in accordance with current regulations. Therefore, a violation shall be issued for failure to restore the well site nine months post-plugging, in accordance with the 3/07/2019 COA.

OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Diversified Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-16
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 859414
Permit API: 051-23989
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-16
Comments: On 08/16/19 at approximately 1000 hours I, along with Environmental Trainee Jessica Morton, conducted a routine complete inspection of the site. The Act 9 sign was in place and the site was well vegetated. The access road was heavily washed out and requires maintenance. The brine tanks were heavily corroded and had poor structural integrity. On each brine tank end cap plugs were not present (see photographs). Multiple holes were observed in both brine tanks. The interior of brine tank 2 was visible through a large hole. Brine tank 2 contained fluid. The Department requests fluid levels from the tanks be provided. The brine tanks were surrounded by an earthen dike. The dike was breached, allowing rain water or any released fluids to escape. The dike did not provide 110% capacity. A container of fluid was observed under the GPU. The Department requests Diversified identify the contents of the container. Diversified failed to notify the Department of tank deficiencies within 3 days of discovery and failed to address and remedy the deficiencies contrary to 78A57(i). The Department requests 1 year (12 months) of brine tank inspections per 78A57(i) be provided to the Department. To achieve compliance the brine tanks must be replaced or remedied in accordance with manufacturer's specifications and applicable engineering design criteria. If the tanks are replaced adherence to chapter 78A regulations regarding secondary containment will be necessary.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Bull Run Resources Llc in Wetmore Twp, McKean County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-06-29 to Bull Run Resources Llc in Wetmore Twp, McKean county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Bull Run Resources Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-29
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 887753
Permit API: 083-54017
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-29
Comments: The operator contacted Brian Ayers to report multiple spills at the Collins Pine 22 well site the morning of 6/29/2020. This inspection was performed as a complaint inspection to CID #350759. The operator was intending to perform an injection test on this well for a proposed injection well permit. They had a 500 barrel laydown tank on location that was filled with brine over the course of several days prior to the test. The operator noted on arriving at the site 6/29 that the site was wet, and then was able to see that the tank was actively leaking brine. They were able to contact a vac truck operator who sent trucks to empty the tank. A mini excavator was used to dig a small trench on the north side of the site. In the interim, the operator hooked a hose from the tank to drain into the well in order to reduce the level of the tank. The packer in the well failed, which allowed oil to be displaced and flow out the backside of the packer string and onto the ground. The operator noticed the discharge and immediately shut the well in and ceased flowing water. They had a mini excavator on site and dug another interceptor trench in the access road to cut off oil from flowing further down gradient toward Route 6. 1-2 barrels of oil was estimated to have been released from this well. At the time of this inspection, the operator had determined that 3" of water had drained from the full tank prior to discovery of the leak, which occurred at approximately 10 am. Further leaking occurred during the time between discovery and the emptying of the tank at approximately 2 PM. The total loss of brine is estimated to be between 5 and 10 barrels. Various areas surrounding the tank were tested with a soil EC meter, which read between 15 mS and >20 mS. Oil was all contained within the trench or puddles on the location, with no threat of further contamination. The operator intends to have a rolloff container on site this evening and begin to scrape up the contaminated soil on site, starting with the area contaminated with crude oil. A vac truck will be on site should extra encountered.

Comments: On 5/13/21 a site inspection of the Rinkhoff Agricultural Enterprises LLC 7N5 was conducted to follow-up on a previous inspection (IR:3176993) conducted on 4/2/21. North of the intersection of the access road to the Rinkhoff Enterprises 5N2 and 5N3 well sites, water was observed flowing and causing accelerated erosion on the access road that leads to the 7N5 (Photos #2-#5). Violation 102.22(a) is being issued for failure to stabilize the site and for accelerated erosion. Violation of 105.47(b) is being issued for failure to remove the culverts.

Violation ID: 964819
Permit API: 083-57144
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/20/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8234379
Permit API: 113-20482
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Elkland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/20/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of at least 5 gallons of produced fluid. Upon arrival I met with Creston Environmental representatives and with Mike Deming of Chesapeake (Expand).While removing secondary containment puddled fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered adjacent to the northern side of the 5HC well cellar. This location is shown on the right side of the well in Photo 1 and in Photo 3. Upon further investigation a hole was discovered in the containment in that area. After discovering the fluid a vac truck was used to remove the fluid and two sumps were started on the northern and southern sides of the wellhead. The sumps encountered additional fluid at around 2.5 feet deep. Fluid has continued to be removed from the sumps. Creston provided conductivity readings for the removed fluid. The initial puddle was 1,280 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The fluid collecting in the sumps was around 14,780 uS/cm on the northern side and 10,446 uS/cm on the southern side. Soil conductivity for the pad surface beyond the sump its self ranged between 89 and 238 uS/cm. There did not appear to be any impacts on the other exposed portions of the pad or the surrounding area. There were no seeps or standing water observed in the area around the pad including in the PCSM.The sumps will be expanded to facilitate monitoring and removal of additional fluid. There will be screening and fluid removal throughout the flowback period. After flowback equipment is removed further characterization and remediation will be completed under Act 2 per Mike Deming. DEP will conduct followup inspections over the coming days and weeks to additionally asses the stability and state of the impacted and downgrade areas.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). The violations may be closed after completion of Act 2 remediation.

Inspection Date: 6/26/2023
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Seneca's Covington Pad R well site in Covington Township, Tioga County on 06/26/2023 at 0950. The weather was 75 degrees with overcast skies. Hydraulic stimulation activities were taking place onsite at the time of inspection. Seneca safety personnel Tighe Truman was onsite at the time of inspection.On 6/25/2023 at 0100 hours Tighe Truman of Seneca Resources notified the DEP that "Beimel Trucking was off-loading to tanks when pop-off relief valve failed spilling approximately 10 gallons of produced water to gravel. Vac truck used to recover liquid; impacted gravel scraped up and placed in bucket." The resulting spray of production fluid in front of the sites temporary storage tank offload area was estimated to be 10 gallons and encompassed roughly a 15 ft span in front of the offload area (picture 4). Steps were then taken to immediately clean the spill involving vacuuming the fluid on the pad surface and than removing impacted and stained materials from this area and storing them within the secondary containment of the temporary storage tanks until proper disposal (picture 5). The six wells onsite were undergoing hydraulic fracturing activities. Lined timber mats remain in place for the hydraulic fracturing operations. Temporary storage tanks were labeled and placed within secondary containment onsite. An Act 9 sign remains at the entrance to the site. Straw, Erosion Control Blanket (ECB), and silt sock remain in place around the pad site. Areas surrounding the pad remain stabilized as they establish vegetation. Post- Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls remain in place. No evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation leaving the site was observed at the time of inspection. Based on the findings of this inspection and Seneca's timely remediation of this release, violations of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response from a notification from the operator that on July 18, 2022, an unknown volume of brine, mixed with oil and stormwater, had overflowed the secondary containment. I met with Rick Hall of EQT upon arriving on location. Tobias excavation was also present on location as well as Creston Environmental. A coiled tubing unit and associated equipment was present on the pad on secondary containment. Damp areas and puddles were present on the north and south sides of the containment. Rick Hall said that the fluid made it off of the containment on both sides. On the north side of the containment the electrical conductivity (EC) in the puddles as measured by the Oakton meter ranged from 651 uS/cm to 3.16 mS/cm. On the south side of the containment each puddle I measured had an EC of greater than 19.99 mS/cm. Toward the end of my inspection, personnel on location had removed a portion of the containment berm on the north side and pulled back the liner approximately 15 feet which revealed that the gravel under the containment was damp. I would estimate the area visibly impacted by the release at approximately 600 square feet.Rick Hall said that the coiled tubing crew should be done by Thursday, July 21st, and then the containment would be removed from the pad surface. Screening of the pad surface where the containment was present would occur at that time, according to Rick Hall. Due to the unknown volume of the release, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation.Violations noted.

I was accompanied by Laura Grada and Ralph Bard (PA DEP).The spill report indicated that a Chemical tote tipped over and released about 25 gallons of defoamer onto well pad gravel. Groundwater/storm drains dont seem to be impacted. SPSI in Washington en route for remediation, absorbent pads have been applied to spill area. Not sure when spill occurred, caller assumed sometime during the storm Saturday evening. It was noted that the spill occurred on 03/07/2026, or sometime over the weekend.I called Range Resources representative Nate Smiell on 03/10/2026 for information about the spill. It was noted that the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) was put on site, the spill was fully remediated, and the container was placed onto secondary containment. The operator submitted a photo of where the spill originated within the tan container (Photo 17). It was also shared that a summary email was being submitted for the spill.On 03/10/2026, at 12:27 pm, the operator submitted information regarding the spill that was reported to the Department on 03/09/2026: "As reported to the PADEP hotline at 1:55 PM on 3/9/2026.Burnsworth S and T Unit 10H (37-125-28884)93 Penn Hill RoadAmity, PA 15311Amwell Township, Washington CountyOn 3/9/2026 at 12:42 PM, while conducting a site check, a lease operator identified a chemical injection tote on its side. It appears that recent high winds blew the unit over and a portion of the contents were released from the fill cap vent. An estimated 25 gallons of defoamer released and was contained to the graveled well pad. Specialized Professional Services Inc. (SPSI) responded to the location and remediated the impacted areas placing the material into roll-off boxes for disposal. Disposal documents will be sent to you as part of the closure summary.Range intends to remediate this release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1)".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and the SDS for the spilled material were on site. The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan was not observed (Photos 1, 2). It was unclear if the SDS was on site before and during the spill incident.I observed two unlabeled roll-offs on site (Photos 3, 4). I recommend labeling the roll-offs.The impacted area appeared to have been excavated and remediated. The area appeared to be approximately 25 x 20 feet in size (Photos 5-10).The source of the spilled material originated within the tan container, which was placed on secondary containment. The labeling of the container did not match the SDS. I observed an absorbent pad within the containment (Photos 11-14).An additional container was within the impacted area. The labeling of this container did not appear to be the same as the tan container (spill origin). This container appeared to be double walled and does not require secondary containment (Photos 15, 16).Violations of 78a54 and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill.

Inspection Date: 8/13/2025
Comments: On August 13, 2025, the Department conducted a Site Restoration inspection of Diversified's Yelenick 2 plugged well following a Well Site Restoration Submission the Department received on 7/22/2025. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 10/24/2024, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 7/24/2025 in accordance with current regulations.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a mailbox and locked gate at the plugged well site's access road entrance. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed a Well Control and Disposal Plan as well as an Erosion and Sediment Control Plan. The beginning portion of the access road was observed to be graveled, however the remaining portion of the access road was observed to be restored and exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Upon inspection of the plugged well site, the Department observed the site to be nearing its 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth requirement with seed and mulch spread throughout its slightly less vegetated areas. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the vegetatie cover at this plugged well site to ensure it reaches its 70% uniform and adequate cover requirement. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed and no erosion and sediment control features were observed to be installed on site and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the plugged well. A pipeline riser was observed to still be present on site, the Department recommends any equipment not necessary for production of the well be removed from the site.Based on today's inspection, the Well Site Restoration Report submission is being denied due to the access road not being fully restored and the well site not yet exhibiting its 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth requirement. The Department recommends the Operator resubmit the WSRR within 60 days after restoration following the instructions for completing form 8000-PM-OOGM0075.In addition, based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of plugging completion.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an inspection app IT error.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: HARPER CROSBY HOLDINGS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/06/2024
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8178615
Permit API: 129-26206
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/06/2024
Comments: On March 6, 2024, inspection conducted in response to a complaint (CTS-374226) on the Terence Shaffer 1-P041 well in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On 03/04/2026, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the Cashdollar Well Site.The following was observed:I observed accelerated erosion on the access road. Near the upper portion of the access road, sediment laden water was traveling towards the adjacent vegetation. It appeared to end within the brush. I observed accumulated road fines and gravel within the vegetation (Photos 1-6). Unconventional: No

Comments: On April 9 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Ackerman 2 OG Well. This well is under Consent Order and Agreement (COA) 407094. The well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department was unable to locate a restoration plan onsite. Therefore, the Department was unable to compare the well site to the restoration plan, however, the Department was able to assess the access road and well site for permanent stabilization and vegetative growth.Upon inspection of the access road, it appeared to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the former well site, the Department observed an above ground monument for the reportedly plugged well. No other production equipment was observed on site. There were no observed leaks at the surface in the area surrounding the well monument. The well site did not appear to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage (photo 4). The Department did not observe any erosion and sedimentation controls installed on site. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to have E and S controls installed as well as failure to have an E and S plan onsite.
